messages:
Henry Cho: Need to lock activation definition for the lifecycle sprint today so Eng can finalize events + Growth can align messaging. Options on the table:
1) first 2xx completion (first_request_success)
2) first streaming success (first_streaming_success)
3) first dashboard view (dashboard_viewed)

What’s the primary metric for “activation within 72h”? Reply w/ +1 and why. Also call out any gotchas (false positives, instrumentation risk).

Marissa Cole: From a product perspective, I’d avoid “dashboard_viewed” as the primary. It’s nice, but it’s not the “I made inference work” moment. It’s also easier to drive with a banner click without real value.

Marissa Cole: Between 2xx vs streaming: 2xx completion is the least opinionated / broadest. Streaming is important but adds edge cases (client disconnects, SDK-specific behavior). I’d make streaming a secondary milestone.

Ben Carter: +1 to Marissa. Growth needs a metric that reflects “they got value.” If we pick streaming as primary, we’ll bias toward a smaller subset (and punish folks using embeddings/rerank or non-streaming).

Ben Carter: Also retargeting copy is “make your first successful call in minutes.” That maps cleanly to first 2xx completion.

Tyler Benson: On attribution joins: first 2xx completion is most robust to capture consistently. We can stitch campaign_touch -> event reliably. Streaming success has more missingness depending on how we detect it.

Tyler Benson: If we do pick 2xx, can we ensure it excludes the “test connection” / health check stuff? I don’t want us counting ping calls from the quickstart template.

Paula Mendes: From telemetry side: “first 2xx completion” is the safest primitive. We already emit most of it server-side. Streaming success requires client-side + server-side correlation and we’ve had bugs where we never get the final “completed” event if the client drops.

Paula Mendes: Suggestion: Primary activation event = first_inference_success (server observed) where:
- response_status in 200..299
- endpoint in {chat.completions, completions, embeddings, rerank}
- output_tokens > 0 OR (for embeddings) embedding_vector_count > 0
- exclude internal health routes and docs examples that hit /status

Paula Mendes: Then define secondary milestones:
- first_streaming_success (received first token chunk + stream not immediately aborted)
- dashboard_viewed (latency/cost page or model route page)

Logan Wright: +1. Also naming: please don’t call it “first_2xx” in the taxonomy. We should keep it semantic: `inference_request_succeeded` with properties.

Logan Wright: The schema question: do we track “activation within 24h/72h” as a derived metric or as a separate event? (Prefer derived in analytics, not a new event.)

Logan Wright: Re: false positives: 2xx can still be “bad” if the model returned an error object in JSON but we surfaced 200. Do we ever do that? (I think we return non-2xx for policy/validation errors.)

Marissa Cole: We should keep it derived. Otherwise we’ll end up with “activation_v1” / “activation_v2” events living forever.

Sana Farid: Stats lens: if we choose streaming as primary, sample size shrinks and variance goes up. Also we’ll systematically undercount Python users who don’t enable streaming by default.

Sana Farid: I’m good with: Primary = inference_request_succeeded within 72h of signup (or api_key_created?) + report time-to-first-success distribution. Secondary = first_streaming_success and dashboard_viewed as leading indicators for D7.

Henry Cho: Good point on “within 72h of signup” vs “within 72h of key creation.” Which anchor is better? PM-412 asks for milestone(s).

Paula Mendes: For the sprint we’re trying to move signup->value. Anchor on signup is the cleanest for GTM. But we should slice by “created API key” since that’s the first hard step.

Tyler Benson: +1 anchor on signup. That’s what email/retargeting targeting uses.

Logan Wright: We can compute:
- Activation_72h = user had `api_key_created` AND `inference_request_succeeded` within 72h of signup
- Time-to-first-success (TTFS) = min(succeeded_ts) - signup_ts

Logan Wright: Just be explicit: if someone succeeds without an API key event (edge case: org admin already created key), we shouldn’t drop them. We can define activation as succeed within 72h; and report a separate “key_created_rate” as funnel step.

Marissa Cole: Agree. There are cases where users are invited to an org and already have access. We should not fail them on a missing key event.

Jada Williams: Implementation note: console experiment bucketing is per user_id. If we define activation as server-side succeeded, we can keep assignment consistent and avoid client SDK drift.

Jada Williams: Also for streaming: we can emit `stream_first_token_received` in console/SDK, but it’s flaky across SDKs. Would rather keep it secondary for now.

Henry Cho: OK sounds like alignment is:
Primary activation metric (sprint): % of new signups with at least one successful inference request (2xx completion) within 72h.
Secondary milestones: first_streaming_success, dashboard_viewed (latency/cost), billing_added, route_created.

Henry Cho: Any objections if we define “successful inference request” as server-observed completion with non-zero output (or embeddings count > 0), excluding health checks?

Ben Carter: No objections. Please make sure embeddings/rerank count so we’re not chat-only.

Sana Farid: Works for me. For reporting, let’s also track “activation within 24h” as early sensitivity + TTFS p50/p75. (Primary still 72h.)

Logan Wright: Works. Please include properties so we can slice:
- model
- sdk_language (if known)
- endpoint_type (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank)
- is_streaming_requested
- region
- error_category (for failures, separate event)

Paula Mendes: Re “non-zero output”: make sure we don’t exclude valid but short outputs (e.g., a single token). So >0 is fine.

Marissa Cole: +1. And let’s not make dashboard_viewed part of activation. We can use it as an intermediate step for nudges.

Henry Cho: Decision locked then.

Henry Cho: Follow-ups:
- Logan: update event taxonomy doc with `inference_request_succeeded` (canonical) + required properties; also confirm naming for streaming event.
- Paula: align with ENG-2841 on server-side emission + any backfill needs.
- Sana: update analysis plan w/ 72h primary, 24h secondary, TTFS distribution + slices.
- Tyler/Ben: update sprint tracker + email KPI language to match.

Henry Cho: I’ll update PM-412 with the decision + rationale (streaming too narrow/flaky; dashboard too easy to game).

Logan Wright: Will do. I’ll also add a note re: derived “activation” metric definition in the taxonomy doc so there’s no ambiguity.

Paula Mendes: I’ll ping Jin Woo / Jada on the minimal schema validation so we don’t ship events missing model/endpoint. :thumbsup:

Tyler Benson: I’ll adjust UTM attribution dashboard to anchor on signup_ts and show activation_24h/72h by campaign. Thanks all.

Marissa Cole: Thanks. Can someone also call out in the PRD that “activation” is not “first dashboard view” so we don’t re-litigate this next week? :joy:

Henry Cho: Yep adding that explicitly.

(automated) Linear Bot: Henry Cho updated PM-412: “Activation metric definition” (status: In Review)

Ben Carter reacted with :white_check_mark:

Sana Farid reacted with :+1:

Logan Wright: One more tiny thing: what about “first_success” when the request is to a deprecated model alias that auto-falls back? Still a success, but we should record `resolved_model` vs `requested_model` so we can see confusion.

Paula Mendes: Great call. I’ll add `requested_model` + `resolved_model` to the properties list (server knows both).

Henry Cho: Perfect. Closing thread unless new issues come up.
